fact: The nonnegative-sum and ε arguments remain valid when ∑ρ_i is infinite: they imply ∑ρ_i≥1 and ∑ρ_i^s≥δ^(s-1).
justification: If A=∑ρ_i is finite and A<1, choosing ε=(1−A)/2 contradicts 1≤A+ε; if A=∞ its lower bound is immediate. Let B=∑ρ_i^s and c=δ^(s−1)>0. The termwise comparison gives c∑_{i∈K}ρ_i≤B for every finite index set K. If B is finite, division by c shows B/c is an upper bound of all these finite sums, so A≤B/c by the definition of their supremum, yielding B≥cA≥c. If B=∞ the conclusion is immediate. This expands exactly the displayed partial-sum argument, without invoking convergence of the possibly infinite sum.
